LESSON: READING 15.4.1 POETRY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.4: Reading 15.4.1 Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 15.4.1 Poetry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why would you use a poem instead of a story to pass information?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the subject matter of a poem

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 15.4.1 POETRY
This lesson teaches Reading 15.4.1 Poetry for Grade 7 ENGLISH.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify the subject matter of a poem
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 15.4.1 Poetry using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 15.4.1 Poetry above.
2. Explain Reading 15.4.1 Poetry to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 15.4.1 Poetry.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 15.4.1 Poetry with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 15.4.1 Poetry important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why would you use a poem instead of a story to pass information?
2. What makes a poem interesting to read?
3. What kind of ideas can one convey using a poem?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the subject matter of a poem

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
